thread:
Alex: kicked off a replay vs synthetic comparison focused on the kernel-selection path + KV eviction overlap. quick summary below.
Maria: nice — which model and replay set?
Alex: customer-replay A (mixed lengths, heavy prefix reuse). model: redwood-open-7b-quant. fed both to the replay harness and to a synthetic driver I wired up (variable-seqlen shoelace driver).
Tim: shoelace driver? give a one-liner
Alex: sure
```bash
# run synthetic load with variable seq lengths and controlled prefix reuse
./perf_runner --driver shoelace --model redwood-open-7b-quant --qps 350 --seq-dist "short:0.6,medium:0.3,long:0.1" --prefix-hit 0.45 --duration 20m
```
Maria: thanks. what did you observe?
Alex: two surprising things:
1) p95 token latency regressed ~7-9% on replay vs previous baseline, but synthetic didn't show the same. p50/p99 stable.
2) KV hitrate on replay was 3-5% lower during warmup spikes, and around those moments we saw a flurry of kernel-switch events (mini-kernel selector switching to a fallback kernel) triggered by observed batch-shape mismatches.
Sarah: hmm kernel switches happening while eviction is removing prefixes could cause inconsistent cache reads. did you see any correctness errors or only perf?
Alex: only performance and transient 504s in a few requests (very rare). logs show eviction loop holding LRU lock while kernel selector tries to migrate a batch -> waiting on same page table structures. not a logic bug in KV contents, but a contention/latency amplification.
Tim: can you paste the small log snippet where the kernel selector and eviction overlap?
Alex: here — trimmed
```
[serving] INFO batch=1234 kernel_select:start candidates=[mini, fallback]
[kvcache] DEBUG evict:start keys=45 lrulock=held
[serving] WARN batch=1234 kernel_select:blocking on lrulock
[kvcache] INFO evict:done reclaimed=12
[serving] INFO kernel_select:switched->fallback latency_ms=12
```
Maria: interesting. so one path is that eviction aggressively holds the LRU lock. we should measure critical section durations across workloads.
Perf-bot: perfbot report attached: replay A vs synthetic shoelace (20m each) — avg_kv_lock_hold_ms: replay=4.8, synth=1.1; kernel_switch_count: replay=72, synth=9; p95_token_latency_ms: replay=72, synth=66
Sarah: we should check whether our kernel selection path asks for any synchronous KV metadata inside the hot path. if it queries metadata while under a global lock that's bad.
Tim: proposed short checklist for a proper apples-to-apples experiment:
- ensure identical seq-length distribution (sampled from replay)
- replay driver should respect original client pacing (burstiness)
- compare warmup phases separately from steady-state (first 5m vs next 15m)
- capture lock-hold histograms for LRU and metadata locks
- instrument kernel-selector to emit batch-shape fingerprint
Alex: did that. attaching quick numbers from today (first 5m vs steady):
```
replay:first5m kv_hit=0.31 p95=98 kernel_switches=38 avg_lru_ms=7.1
replay:steady kv_hit=0.44 p95=66 kernel_switches=34 avg_lru_ms=3.9
synth:first5m kv_hit=0.33 p95=71 kernel_switches=4 avg_lru_ms=1.0
synth:steady kv_hit=0.47 p95=64 kernel_switches=5 avg_lru_ms=1.2
```
Maria: wow steady-state numbers are close for p95 but warmup differs a lot. that suggests replay's burstiness forces kernel selector into more diversity and triggers eviction pressure.
Tim: mitigation ideas:
- make eviction more cooperative (yielding inside long runs)
- avoid holding LRU global lock across I/O or kernel selection
- add a tiny per-batch metadata snapshot to avoid synchronous lookups in selector
Sarah: also consider adding a guarded kernel-switch window during warmup where we delay non-critical kernel migrations until cache warms up. cheaper to trade a little baseline perf for fewer thrash events.
Alex: action items I can take now:
- open perf ticket with logs + perf-bot summary (A -> TICKET-3245)
- add histogram instrumentation for lrulock hold times per op (PR incoming)
- update synthetic driver to replay burst patterns exactly (PR incoming)
- short experiment to test 'cooperative-evict' patch (branch: coop-evict)
Maria: I'll add an eval card to track whether quality (generation tokens) changes with coop-evict vs switch-delay. want to avoid silent regressions.
Tim: I'll review the kernel-selector path for synchronous kv calls and send a small refactor PR.
Alex: for the ticket notes I'll include the shoelace config and the replay snippet and the small log excerpt.
Sarah: schedule a 30m sync tomorrow to review preliminary coop-evict results? :calendar:
Alex: yes, 11am PT works for me. tagging perf-bot to run nightly replay with the coop-evict branch.
perf-bot: scheduled nightly run: replay-A @ 04:00 UTC against branch/coop-evict — results will post in #eng-runtime-summary
Alex: thanks all. TL;DR: replay warmup + kernel-switches + eviction contends causing p95 blips; reproduceable with replay but not naive synthetic; plan: instrument, patch eviction to be cooperative, and re-run apples-to-apples tests.
